original_before_fix_observations.observation: The original delayed baseline published a usable login window after the source was revoked and re-enrolled with the same enabled payload.
The original delivery path accepted a request after its previously authenticated phone pairing had been replaced; the HTTP path discarded the presented pairing token before delivery.
The original delivery path accepted a message matched to the previous sender into a new login window for the replacement sender.
The original Gmail window remained valid after a fresh owner authorization changed authorization_id, even when token contents were unchanged.

oauth_lock_wait_before_fix_proof.unsafe_observation: While waiting for the OAuth account lock, the old checker accepted a cached window after source revocation, window finish, same-value reenrollment or changing the mailbox account.

final_local_validation.final_gmail_case_proves: Cancellation during the second OAuth-lock wait rejects the window without any mailbox request; fresh baseline and resolution still work.

semantics: A private enrollment revision binds every login window; replacing or revoking an enrollment invalidates earlier windows even when payloads are identical.
Source publication and window publication are serialized in the established lock order; paired phone token and source replacement commit atomically.
In-flight phone delivery rechecks the presented pairing token and the source/sender revision before acceptance.
Mailboxes bind current enrollment and OAuth authorization identity; a new owner authorization invalidates old windows while ordinary refresh and legacy first refresh remain compatible.
OAuth lock waits reload live window and source authority. Cancellation before Gmail resolution makes no mailbox request.
Legacy mailbox profiles and health-only rechecks preserve compatible active windows. No additional routine owner approval was introduced.
